content.title: About
content.content: Pork is a protein‑rich meat that provides B‑vitamins and essential minerals. Combined with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (such as spinach or kale), the dish gains extra vitamins A, C, K, as well as fiber, minerals and antioxidants. Prepared without potatoes or soy‑based sauce, it suits those limiting gluten and soy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its anti‑cancer properties.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens are rich in chlorophyll and vitamin K.
When paired correctly, protein and vegetables provide a balanced profile of amino acids and micronutrients.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Pork supplies complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: It contains thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Broccoli and carrots provide vitamin C, beta‑carotene and sulforaphane, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: Leafy greens and carrots add dietary fiber, potassium, magnesium and iron, beneficial for heart health and digestion.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: The combination of vitamins A, C and zinc from pork and vegetables helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Some cuts of pork can be high in saturated fat; choose lean cuts and limit added oil.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Pork should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C to destroy pathogens.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pork.

items.title: Interaction with medication
items.content: High vitamin K levels in leafy greens can affect the efficacy of anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté, roast or stew pork with carrots, broccoli and leafy greens. Add a drizzle of olive oil, garlic and your favorite herbs. Serve hot, either with whole‑grain sides or as a standalone plate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw pork refrigerated at ≤4 °C for 2‑3 days; store cooked dishes in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze the meat in sealed bags and keep vegetables in moisture‑controlled bags.
